## Design

### 2026-10-13 – I sketched up what I want the gate to look like and then began prototyping. I looked through a couple of different sensors to detect the cars and decided to go with the ultrasonic sensor because it is

**2.5h**

I sketched up what I want the gate to look like and then began prototyping. I looked through a couple of different sensors to detect the cars and decided to go with the ultrasonic sensor because it is safer than the other option being a laser. I connected some parts on a breadboard and blocked up some code to test the basic system. I couldn't get anything to work on it which could have been because I bought the ultrasonic sensor and LEDs many years ago. I am going to continue trying to get them working and then I'll design the gate and finish the code.

### 2026-10-15 – I designed the basis of my Gaslands Gate in Fusion360. This rough design includes all of the necessary component attachment bits required for my electronics to fit in. I sadly do not have an image bec

**3.5h**

I designed the basis of my Gaslands Gate in Fusion360. This rough design includes all of the necessary component attachment bits required for my electronics to fit in. I sadly do not have an image because it is on my other computer (I'll add images in later entries).
I decided to use a pair of IR beam break detectors instead of an ultrasonic because they detect movement over a singular point, instead of requiring the car to be over both the speaker and microphone. This was also easier to code because it's either outputting a high or low voltage instead of a distance. I think that this will generally be more reliable and work better. I have also not used beam break sensors before.
I blocked up the code for this project, which was very simple. In the RTTTL spot there is the song "Never gonna give you up" as a placeholder that I might change out for something I write if I have time this week. I may also change the LED activation to make it flow smoother if I want.
My next steps are ordering the parts, and making the Gaslands Gate look like it came straight out of the post apocalyptic world where it is set.

### 2026-10-16 – Seeing as the gate is for Gaslands (The game of post apocalyptic vehicular mayhem), it needs to look like it's from the same world. I designed tires, cans, and their groupings so that I can paint them

**2h**

Seeing as the gate is for Gaslands (The game of post apocalyptic vehicular mayhem), it needs to look like it's from the same world. I designed tires, cans, and their groupings so that I can paint them up and conceal the electronics behind them. I also designed a sign for the top of the gate that says "Gaslands". I couldn't find a suitable font so I will use paint to make it look realistic. I made these designs in Tinkercad because I find it easier to design less functional parts there. The main parts for my project are designed in Fusion360.

### 2026-10-17 – In this session, I turned a very basic draft of the gate into the final model. I added holes for the LEDs to fit into, and piping for wires to travel through.

**5h**

In this session, I turned a very basic draft of the gate into the final model. I added holes for the LEDs to fit into, and piping for wires to travel through.

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 171744](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/42c611fc40832382a3a52c9406704392572c1855468113ae7ee5f378716173cd.png)

This project is going to be powered VIA the USB C port on the arduino itself, meaning I will only need 1 port for both power and changing the code if necessary. I modelled a hole for where this is:

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 171417](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/c96a4afa529af6e1750f8a06e54d80dba93745b81168fff99f8bf3ef751b7638.png)

I added some lattices to make it look like it was trussed up with metal bars.

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 174120](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/1bb26d63ffb25374d98c01ce7dfbabb2e2a1d02233d0102cf01f0e8643405063.png)

This has a really cool effect to it, especially when you're up close and looking at the aforementioned piping. I left space at the top for the GASLANDS sign to be. I will have it in two spots. One spot will say GAS and the other will say LANDS. I also split up the model into 4 parts to be printed seperately. (My printer isn't big enough!)

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 175442](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/75c51c96f5c7493e907738622da15d1011a2e83341cfd8b3dfafb9362155a833.png)

(That will be added when I assemble, together with the parts from Tinkercad)

I added a lid to the control panel on the side so that it is contained and can't be seen. I also added holes for the mode switch and the buzzer.

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 181210](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/aee53175ebcf9c8daa1a47aacbdf12ebc88bd86db5620c7a63f7b52723f7b63e.png)

I also did some non-cad stuff like add to the cost documentation and order parts.

I think I am ready to submit this project!
